content.title: About
content.content: The California sushi roll is a popular Western-style roll made with sushi rice, nori, crab meat (or imitation crab), avocado, and cucumber. It is typically served with soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger. The roll is known for its mild flavor and creamy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The roll was created in the 1970s at a California restaurant using imitation crab to keep costs low.
Avocado gives the roll its characteristic buttery taste and adds nutritional value.
The California roll is considered a “Western” adaptation of traditional Japanese sushi, tailored to American palates.
Some variations replace crab with salmon or tuna, but the classic recipe keeps the original ingredients.
Wasabi is often omitted to let the delicate avocado flavor shine.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Avocado provides monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E from avocado acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Cucumber and rice supply fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The roll contains virtually no added sugar, making it suitable for moderate consumption.

items.title: Provides protein
items.content: Crab meat (or its imitation) adds protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Crab meat can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce served with the roll is often high in salt; low‑sodium options are recommended.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: If stored at improper temperatures, the rice can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite its light appearance, the combination of rice, avocado, and crab imitation makes the roll fairly calorie‑dense.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: California rolls are usually eaten with chopsticks, dipped in soy sauce. Add a touch of wasabi if desired and eat pickled ginger between bites to cleanse the palate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rolls in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C, wrapped in plastic film or placed in an airtight container. Consume within 24 hours to maintain rice freshness and nori crispness.
